# Mission 1

## Hallway Analysis

I would say the most uncomfortable behavior is in trial 2, because a person nearby can't predict which direction the robot will go next. For example, in trial 3 during the curved motion,  people can see where the robot will go next.
I would suggest changing v when the robot turns, so it motions will be smoother and more human-like.

## Trial Synthesis

All three trial matched my expected path shapes and turning directions, however odometry results is consistently 10% less than predicted. The largest difference was in trial 3 - odometry results for heading was 1.468 rad instead of 1.6 rad. A possible cause of such behavior can be the robot's speed (the actual speed is lower that commanded due to some reasons). This can be tested by conducting more trials, and measuring if the error stays around 10%.
At the same speed for twice the duration, the straight-line distance would be d = vt = 2* 0.45 =0.9m, or about 0.81m with the same odometry problems

## Compare.Straight

My prediction and ideal model parameters matched, however, the odometry-estimated path is slightly different (predicted: 0.45m, odometry-estimated: 0.403m).
This can be due to the fact that the robot actually moved less than it supposed to (due to the environment conditions or mechanical characteristics of the robot itself). Robot also could travel 0.45 m as it supposed to, but our sensor reported that it travelled only 0.403.
We need to check if that is consistent and the odometry-estimated path is always approximately 10% less than it supposed to be -> we need to run more tests.
Then, we need to check if the robot actually travelled 0.45 m and, additionally, we need to take a look at velocity (commanded and measured).
